evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Hung Up' (released 17 October 2005, produced with Stuart Price): it is built on a sample of 'Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)' (1979). Andersson and Ulvaeus rarely allow samples, and Madonna sent an emissary to Stockholm with a letter asking for permission; they agreed after negotiating a significant share of the royalties.

earlier.title: Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen for the fast, climbing synthesizer riff that opens the ABBA record. On 'Hung Up' it is the hook of the whole song, looped under a steady four-to-the-floor club beat and a ticking clock. Notice how little else Madonna took: one riff, used again and again.

explanation.age13: ABBA's songwriters almost never let anyone sample their music. Madonna sent someone to Stockholm with a letter asking to use the synthesizer riff from 'Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!'. They said yes, and 'Hung Up' went to number one in 41 countries.
explanation.adult: A sample cleared by persuasion and a royalty share, from writers whose refusals are the rule. It links a Swedish pop group to the club-pop line on this map that runs back through Madonna to Nile Rodgers and disco.
